gloss: to cut out; to quarry; to bring up (a topic)

definitions.gloss: to cut out; to quarry; to extract
definitions.explanation: To cut something out from a larger whole, such as cutting stone from a quarry or extracting material.

definitions.gloss: to bring up (a topic); to broach
definitions.explanation: To start talking about something, especially a difficult or delicate subject.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}から{石|いし}を{切|き}り{出|だ}す。
examples.english: They quarry stone from the mountain.

examples.japanese: {話|はなし}を{切|き}り{出|だ}すタイミングが{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's hard to find the right timing to bring up the topic.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{別|わか}れ{話|ばなし}を{切|き}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: She brought up the subject of breaking up.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・{切|き}り{出|だ}す → {切|き}り{出|だ}さない (negative)
・{切|き}り{出|だ}す → {切|き}り{出|だ}して (te-form)
・{切|き}り{出|だ}す → {切|き}り{出|だ}した (past)

FORMATION:
Compound verb: {切|き}る (to cut) + {出|だ}す (to take out, to begin)

USAGE:
Sense 2 (broaching a topic) is more common in everyday conversation:
・{話|はなし}を{切|き}り{出|だ}す (to bring up a topic)
・{本題|ほんだい}を{切|き}り{出|だ}す (to get to the main point)
・なかなか{切|き}り{出|だ}せない (unable to bring oneself to bring it up)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{持|も}ち{出|だ}す - to bring up, to take out
・{言|い}い{出|だ}す - to start saying
